summary: Defined the duties of the Secretary to the President.
Put the Midway Islands under the jurisdiction and control of the Navy Department.
Abolished the land office at Prescott in the Arizona Land District and moved its business to Phoenix.

Barred federal employees who are also notaries public from charging fees for notarial acts done for government business, for fellow employees acting officially, or during their government work hours. Breaking the rule meant immediate dismissal.

Set aside four islands in Stump Lake, North Dakota, totaling 27.39 acres, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds under the Department of Agriculture, to be known as the Stump Lake Reservation.
Moved the land office at Oregon City to Portland.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve certain Minnesota lands for flowage purposes.
Shifted certain lands from the Lakeview Land District in Oregon to the Burns Land District.
Revoked an unnumbered order of February 9, 1905, that had moved the Office of the Commissioner of Railroads to the Department of Commerce and Labor.

Reorganized the Isthmian Canal Commission, calling its performance unsatisfactory. Set quarterly sessions on the Isthmus, a four-member quorum and an Executive Committee, and charged the Commission, under the Secretary of War, with planning and building the canal and running the Panama Railroad.
Modified an order of August 13, 1902, so the Navy Department could discharge, on request, messmen who enlist only for the Naval Academy midshipmen's summer practice cruise.
Abolished the Ironton Land District in Missouri and folded it into the Springfield Land District.
Reserved public lands on the east side of the entrance to Subig Bay, in Bataan Province on Luzon, for military purposes, subject to private rights, approving a Secretary of War recommendation.
Abolished the Marysville Land District and transferred it to the Sacramento Land District.
Abolished the Boonville Land District and transferred it to the Springfield Land District.
Created the Uintah Land District.
Abolished the Akron Land District in Colorado and moved it into the Sterling Land District.
Directed the Department of Commerce and Labor to take charge of lighting and buoying the waters around Guam, and to have the Light-House Establishment prepare cost estimates for Congress.
Canceled Executive Order 302-A of March 10, 1905, and reserved additional lands in its place.
Amended Executive Order 310-C, the Minnesota flowage reservation, to leave out the lands in Louis Zeph's homestead entry.
Reserved government properties in Manila for military use, including the Cuartel Meisic barracks, approving a Secretary of War recommendation.
Added tracts of land at Jolo, Philippine Islands, to the existing military reservation there, subject to private rights, approving a Secretary of War recommendation.
Redrew the boundaries of the military reservation at Zamboanga, Mindanao, amending an earlier 1904 order and reserving the public lands within the new lines, subject to private rights.

Required federal contracts for work in the states and adjoining territories to forbid the use of convicts sentenced to hard labor by state, territorial or municipal courts, unless law provided otherwise.
Changed the boundaries of the Uintah Land District in Utah, issued in the form of a proclamation.

Reserved lands in Alaska for the Army Signal Corps' military telegraph lines: a 100-foot right of way along more than 1,400 miles of line, plus sites for telegraph offices, storehouses, stables and wood reserves such as Central, Chestochena and Copper Center.
Set extra monthly pay for Navy enlisted men detailed as ship's tailors ($10 to $20, depending on the ship's crew size) and as tailor's helpers ($10), with caps on their total pay.
Reserved all of Grass Island in Grays Harbor, Washington, for the harbor's defense.
Amended the 1901 order setting maximum punishments for Army enlisted men, laying out new confinement limits for desertion based on surrender or capture, time served, prior convictions and conspiracy.
Named an international Board of Consulting Engineers, with General George W. Davis as chairman, to meet in Washington on September 1, 1905, and weigh plans for a canal across the Isthmus of Panama.
Put the Department of Commerce and Labor in charge of lights and other navigation aids for Tutuila and the other Samoan Islands east of longitude 171° west.
Reserved waterfront public land at Seward, Alaska, for the Army Signal Corps' military telegraph lines, subject to private rights.

Declared that Army and Navy appointments, transfers and assignments would rest on official department records, not outside influence. Officers who sought outside backing would be barred from the advancement they sought; eyewitness accounts of unrecorded bravery could still be submitted.
Took about 28 acres out of the Fort Bayard military reservation in New Mexico and placed them under the Secretary of the Interior for disposal.
Gave Special Panama Railroad Commissioner Joseph L. Bristow until August 15, 1905, to finish his report, with expenses, $15 a day, and an extra $2,500, paid by the Isthmian Canal Commission.
Redrew the Fort Gibbon military reservation in Alaska, adding a strip along the east side and Bull Island in the Yukon River and turning excluded lands over to the Interior Department.
Moved the Gila Land District office from Tucson, Arizona, to Phoenix.
Added certain Utah lands to the Uintah Indian Reservation on the Acting Interior Secretary's recommendation, despite an earlier application by the State of Utah for water rights from Rock Creek.
Added more lands within the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah to protect the Indians' water rights, approving the Acting Interior Secretary's recommendation.
Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation on what to do with the Fort Shaw Indian School Reservation in Montana.
Reserved land on Revillagigedo Island, Alaska, as a site for a lighthouse depot.
Made lands the government bought from Indians on Agate Passage, once part of the Port Madison Indian Reservation in Washington, into a military reservation for fortifications.
Reserved certain lands for the Pueblo Indians of the Pueblo of Santa Clara in New Mexico.
Abolished the Ashland and Eau Claire land districts in Wisconsin and moved them into the Wausau Land District.
Revoked an 1852 executive order that had reserved certain Michigan lands for lighthouse purposes.
Reserved Santa Barbara Island, California, for lighthouse purposes.
Reserved parcels of newly reclaimed harbor land in Manila for military purposes.
Excused Washington Navy Yard employees from work on Labor Day, September 4, 1905.

Set pay for each member of the advisory board of engineers on Panama Canal plans: $5,000 on completion of the report, $15 a day in expenses and travel costs, with Generals Davis and Abbott's allowance raised to offset their retired pay.
Reserved land on Gravina and False islands in Alaska for lighthouse purposes.
Redrew the military reservation at Fort San Pedro near Iloilo, Panay, amending a 1903 order so it covers only the public lands within the new bounds.

Required that the Medal of Honor be presented with formal ceremony, by the President or his representative in Washington when practicable; otherwise as the Chief of Staff directs, or by a division or higher commander on campaign.
Reserved public lands at Safety Harbor and Old Woman, Alaska, for the Army Signal Corps' military cable and telegraph lines, subject to private rights.
Discontinued the western land district in Oklahoma Territory, with its office at Kingfisher, and merged its lands, business and records into the eastern district at Guthrie.
Set aside Passage Key, an island near the mouth of Tampa Bay, Florida, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds under the Department of Agriculture, named the Passage Key Reservation.
Reserved the Siskiwit (Menagerie) islands off Isle Royal in Lake Superior, Michigan, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, to be called the Siskiwit Islands Reservation.
Reserved the Huron Islands near Lake Superior's south shore in Michigan as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds under the Department of Agriculture, named the Huron Islands Reservation.
Abolished the Grand Forks Land District in North Dakota and moved it into the Devils Lake Land District.
Reduced the Black Hills Forest Reserve in South Dakota, issued in the form of a proclamation.
Reserved additional California lands in connection with the Point Sal lighthouse reservation.
Gave qualified Navy enlisted men on submarine torpedo boats $1 extra for each day spent submerged under way, on top of their $5 monthly submarine pay, up to $15 a month.
Set aside Breton Island and the Old Harbor and Freemason islands in Louisiana as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, to be known as the Breton Island Reservation.
Reserved public land at the western end of the Mesa near Zamboanga, Mindanao, as a target range for the Zamboanga post.
Abolished the Bent Land District in Colorado and moved it into the Valley Land District, with its office at Pueblo.
Shrank the St. Michael Military Reservation in Alaska and transferred the excluded lands to the Interior Department.
Changed one word in the August 31, 1905, pay order for the Panama Canal's Advisory Board of Engineers, from "report" to "work," so foreign members could be paid before heading home.
Reserved certain lands in California for lighthouse purposes.
Reserved public lands on Chilkat Inlet, Alaska, to supply water to Fort William H. Seward.
Abolished the Sidney Land District in Nebraska and moved it into the Western Land District at North Platte.
Reserved public lands at Keystone, Alaska, for a military telegraph.
Let the Isthmian Canal Commission hold its January 1, 1906, session in Washington instead of on the Isthmus so it could consider the advisory board of engineers' report.

Answering a National Association for the Study and Prevention of Tuberculosis resolution, appointed the Army, Navy and Public Health surgeons general to plan an inquiry into sanitary conditions in government offices and workshops.
Abolished the Stockton Land District in California and moved it into the Sacramento Land District.
Created the Jamestown Ter-Centennial Commission, made up of the Secretaries of the Treasury, War and Navy, to carry out the 1905 act for a celebration near Jamestown on Hampton Roads.
Withdrew Minnesota lands, including islands in Aitkin, Pokegama and Leyton lakes, from sale for the War Department's reservoir system at the headwaters of the Mississippi River.
Temporarily withdrew public lands at Diamond Head, Kupikipikio Point and Punchbowl Hill in Hawaii for military use until surveys decide what permanent reservations are needed.
Shifted certain lands from the Bismarck Land District to the Fargo Land District in North Dakota.
Redrew the Fort Washakie military reservation in Wyoming to match a new survey, leaving out land used for Indian school buildings and keeping the Indians' rights to the land.
Abolished the military reservation on Malagi (Malahi) Island in Laguna de Bay, Luzon, as useless, returning it to the Philippine government for the inhabitants' benefit.
Reserved Yes Lake (Lake McDonald), Yes Bay, Back Bay and strips of shoreline in Alaska as a salmon hatchery site, keeping Native rights to fish and gather fuel.
Set aside block 77 in the Randlett, Utah, town site for the Protestant Episcopal Church to use for missionary and cemetery purposes benefiting the Ute Indians.
Allowed John H. Smith to be hired as a laborer in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without following the usual laborer regulations.
Amended paragraph 660 of the 1896 Consular Regulations so gold or silver bullion is not counted as money or currency.
Amended the civil service rules to require certification of laborers who do the work of classified employees.
Allowed thirteen temporary clerks compiling the Philippine census in the Bureau of the Census to be permanently appointed, since the Civil Service Commission could not certify qualified eligibles.
Ordered a commission to investigate the naturalization of aliens under existing laws and report by November 15, 1905.
Set the pay of the Consultative Board of Architects.
Amended the civil service rules so Post Office Department cashiers and finance clerks hired without examination gain competitive status only on the Postmaster-General's recommendation.
Allowed S. F. Scott, Jr., to be reinstated in the Post-Office Service despite the time limit on reinstatement.
Excepted all firemen on War Department torpedo planters from civil service examination.
Waived the three-year Philippine service requirement so Edward H. Hareford could transfer to forest assistant in the Department of Agriculture.
Allowed a laborer to be hired, without examination, to drive the Treasury Secretary's carriage.
Allowed John Ball Osborne to be appointed chief of the State Department's Bureau of Trade Relations without regard to civil service rules.
Allowed Chauncey O. Howard to move from an excepted special examiner post in the Bureau of Pensions to a similar post that is not excepted.
Allowed William J. Humphreys to be appointed professor of meteorological physics in the Weather Bureau without examination.
Waived civil service rules for five Isthmian Canal Service appointments in New Orleans and Washington, D.C., two of them transfers from the Isthmus.
Allowed Mary T. Waggaman to be appointed a clerk in the Bureau of Labor without regard to civil service rules.
Approved Charles W. Bell's appointment as finance clerk at the Lowell, Massachusetts, post office, since it was authorized before the job became competitive.
Extended Allen Hazen's temporary job as consulting engineer on the Washington filtration plant, at $275 a month, for up to seven months from August 31, 1905.
Allowed Henry Summers to be appointed a clerk in the New York pension agency without examination.
Allowed temporary clerk Gertrude Weaver to be permanently appointed a clerk in the Signal Service without examination.
Allowed Charles W. Spicer to be hired without examination in the Bureau of the Census for experimental work on tabulating machines.
Excepted a private secretary or confidential clerk to the Post Office Department's purchasing agent from civil service examination.
Allowed Mrs. May R. Proctor to be appointed in the Government Printing Office without examination.

Waived the usual civil service removal procedure for officers and employees on the Isthmus of Panama, while requiring the reasons for removal to be recorded and shared with the Civil Service Commission on request.
Allowed John B. Goff and D. P. Wells to be appointed assistant forest rangers in the Forest Service without examination.
Excepted one private secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey from civil service examination.
Directed the Civil Service Commission to help set up competitive exams, open to District of Columbia residents, for clerical jobs in the Recorder of Deeds office in Washington.
Allowed Edward McCauley to be appointed chief of the Post Office Department's Redemption Division without examination, given his experience as chief clerk of the Census Bureau.

Brought hiring at Indian warehouses under the civil service rules and laborer regulations, giving current employees other than unskilled laborers classified status but requiring an exam before any transfer.
Excepted one tobacco examiner and one tea examiner in the Customs Service at Chicago from civil service examination.
Allowed S. H. Alexander of North Carolina, a classified laborer in the Post Office Department, to be appointed to a permanent clerical position.
Excepted cooks from civil service examination when the Commission judges competitive exams impractical.
Allowed Edna M. Peltz to be permanently appointed to a clerical position in the Pension Office without examination.
Allowed Emily L. Genella to be reappointed in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing despite the civil service year limit.
Allowed Mrs. Mary E. Griffin to be reappointed in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing despite the civil service year limit.

Rewrote the civil service exceptions for the Isthmian Canal Commission, exempting all Isthmus jobs except clerks, bookkeepers, stenographers, typists, doctors, trained nurses and draftsmen, and barring noncompetitive appointees from transferring to competitive posts.
Allowed Dr. Walter R. Brinckerhoff to be appointed head of the leprosy hospital station and laboratory in Hawaii, subject to a noncompetitive examination.
Allowed Mary H. Donnelly to be reinstated as a clerk in the Office of the Chief of Ordnance despite the year limit on reinstatement.
Allowed Charles S. Brown to be appointed an inspector in the Government Printing Office if he passes a noncompetitive examination.
Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission until September 2, 1906, to finish its work.
Allowed Joseph Fought to be promoted from classified laborer to clerk in the Treasury Department, citing his earlier War Department clerkship and gallant Civil War service.
